title: Bad day learning Korean? Save this one 🥺 #learnkorean
caption:
Two Korean lines for the days it all goes wrong:

괜찮아 (gwaen-cha-na) = It's okay.
잘하고 있어 (jal-ha-go i-sseo) = You're doing well.

Both are casual, for friends and family, or for yourself. To someone older, say 괜찮아요 and 잘하고 있어요.

Day 1, you couldn't even write 가 (ga). Now, even your mistakes are whole sentences. That counts.

pinnedComment: Which Korean word gives you the hardest time? 👇
alt: A needle-felted desk at night. Red X marks land on a notebook while a coral felt mascot lies flat on it. The window opens and felt letters float in: 괜찮아 (It's okay). Wind flips the notebook back to page one, where 가 나 다 are shaky pencil letters. Back on today's page, even the mistakes are whole sentences. It writes a new line and gets another X. Then the first page and today's page lie open side by side, felt letters arrive — 잘하고 있어 (You're doing well) — and a tear rolls down. The letters settle onto the page and a pencil writes 잘하고 있어 on a new line, with no X.
